research.title: Chemical equation
research.note: Supplies the About page facts: what an equation lists, that every element must appear equally often on both sides, that no number in front of a formula means one, and that Jean Beguin drew the first one in 1615. The About panel also reads this article's summary live when it is opened and shows the day it was read.

research.title: Periodic table
research.note: Supplies the About page facts on Mendeleev's 1869 table, the 118 known elements and the 18 groups and the periods the layout uses.

research.title: Haber process
research.note: Supplies the About page fact that the Haber-Bosch process is the main industrial route to ammonia, from nitrogen in the air and hydrogen over an iron catalyst. It also underlies the Fertiliser works route in chapter 5.

research.title: PubChem Periodic Table
research.by: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), US National Library of Medicine
research.note: Element cards read this service's JSON table live when a card is opened (atomic mass, group block, state and year of discovery) and name the day it was read. A bundled snapshot of the same table, read on the date shown, stands in when the service cannot be reached; the proofs use only the snapshot.

inspiration.title: Chemical equation balancing exercises
inspiration.note: The puzzle form is the textbook one: count each element on both sides and adjust the whole-number coefficients until they match. Reaction Bench keeps the form, proves every answer with an exact solver, and turns each solved equation into a flask on a shelf and a tile on a periodic table.

inspiration.title: Unpacking
inspiration.note: The calm, untimed feel of putting things where they belong and watching a collection fill in.

other.title: Pyodide
other.note: Runs the game's Python rules, balancer and ledger in the browser, so there is no server and no build step.

other.title: Hand-drawn flasks and atoms
other.note: Every flask, atom chip and table tile is drawn as SVG by code. Nothing is generated by an image tool or downloaded. The compound names, the one-line element uses and the short facts about each reaction were written for this game.
